recipes.name: Ed Zieba's Famous Family Pork Chops

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Season pork chops with seasoned salt; place in a glass baking dish. Arrange onion slices on chops; pour water into the dish. Cover with aluminum foil.

Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour. Reduce the oven temperature to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Continue baking until an instant-read thermometer inserted into centers reads 145 degrees F (63 degrees C), about 30 minutes more.

raw_recipe.headline: Ed Zieba's Famous Family Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Ed Zieba's famous family pork chops are my dad's recipe. With only four ingredients — pork chops, salt, onions, and water— they fall-off-the-bone tender.

review.reviewBody:
this is tami, the recipe submitter...thankx for all the comoments, however for those who said it had not much flavor, i can see why, just by looking at the picture that someone put up on this. it looks NOTHING like what this is supposed to. i need to put one up i think:)

it should come out looking very very VERY juicy, the pan over half full with an orangy liquid to where the onions soak up this color and are almost melted. if the onions are piled on top and still white when you take it fromt he oven, you didnt add enough season all, or water. this dish does not need anything else but that, unless something else suits your palate:)

enjoy!

Great recipe as is! So moist and flavorful! Because I like to play around with recipes, I made this a second time with a few changes and it came out really good as well: used a mix of chicken broth & white wine instead of water, peeled and thinly sliced some apples to layer the bottom of the glass pan before placing the chops in it, and added garlic powder & a pork rib rub to the seasoning. Deliciousl!!

Excellent. I used this wonderful recipe as a guide, but modified it to suit my preferences. I did use thick chops & put them a quick 15 minute marinade before cooking chops. I rinsed the chops afterward & patted dry. Then I seasoned the chops as directed & sautéed them before baking them in the oven. Instead of water as the liquid, I used reserved marinade combined with white wine. After baking for the first hour, I added a bit of chicken broth. Additionally, I made a mushroom gravy to top the chops. These turned out to be easy & delicious! I will make them again.

I used boneless, so the meat was a little dry. But if I had used bone-in, that would probably have not been the case. The meat was TENDER. It was fabulous. I actually browned the chops first for a couple of minutes on each side in a cast iron pan on the stove. Also, used chicken broth instead of water for extra flavor. Then just put them in the oven in the same cast iron pan, with lid. Then when they came out, I removed the chops and added a little corn starch to the juices to make a yummy gravy. Very delicious!

The rating here is really for the cooking method. I wasn't able to use a grill, and I didn't want to fry them first, but I modified the cooking method just slightly and they turned out amazing. Marinaded the chops in olive oil, oregano, onion, garlic, salt, pepper, and sugar for 4 hours. Prepared the dish with half water, half Worcestershire sauce, baked at 350 for 35 minutes, and 300 for 15 minutes. Very juicy, and way easier than using the frying pan.

I was surprised how good the chops were. Very good. Lots of flavor and very moist. I did this in my slow cooker. Four pork chops. 3 onions. Each chop generously salted with the seasoned salt. I added 5 small, waxy gold potatoes that were scrubbed but not peeled. I added more water. Maybe a cup to 1 1/2 cup of water. Only needed a couple of hours on high to cook and I didn't have to heat up the kitchen with my oven. No need to make the A/C work harder. :)

Delicious. I’ve had just like the recipe dictates. Last night I put cream of mushroom soup with 1/2 cup water mixed in it and spooned it on the chops. Then the onions and water as the original recipe says. 
My friend likes gravy so we added brown gravy mix to most of juices from the pan and made gravy. Yummmmm
Very good. I also went and put the pork chops in water and a little salt for about 30 minutes before I started the recipe. Very tender and flavorful.

I have made a similar recipe but I trim the excess fat from my pork chops and season them with season salt, garlic powder and black pepper. Next I put the fat in a heavy skillet and render the grease from the fat. There will only be enough to cover the bottom of the skillet. If not, add enough oil to just cover the bottom of the skillet and flash fry the chops over high heat until they are brown on both sides but not cooked thru. Next I place them in a baking dish, cover them with onions, you decide how many just insure each pork chop has some, add about 2 to 3 tablespoons of water or chicken broth, cover and cook 30 to 45 minutes until tender and succulent. My family calls these "Mama's Pork Chops." Try them they are super easy, really flavorful and very very tender and succulent, not dry. I bake them at 350.

These turned out great! Since there are only 2 of us, I used 2 boneless chops and for personal preference used 1/2 water and 1/2 Worcestershire sauce, baked at 400 for 30 minutes and turned the oven down to 300 for another 25 minutes. They were very tender and flavorful. I served with broccoli, cauliflower and carrots in light cheese sauce and fresh strawberries. Great!
Used boneless chops. I didn't have any onions so rubbed garlic in and used BBQ sauce. Cooked for 30 min @400 and for 45 @350. very tender and tasty.
tastes great !

I have tried multiple recipes to get pork chops tender enough for my aging parents. THIS was so tender! I am now experimenting with ingredients. I added a dry packet of French onion soup mix & it was incredible! Thank you for sharing!
I've been making this recipe for at least 15 years. They turn out perfect every time! Tender and falling off the bone. The onions are wonderful! Great simple recipe!

The only changes I made were to add sliced yellow squash and red potatoes cut into eighths on top of the slided onions. My chops were thin so I baked them at 350 for 35 minutes with the foil and water as directed. I would give it for 4 stars for flavor, but it's such an easy and fast dinner and it's easy to sprinkle some Tony's on them so I'm giving it 5.

AWESOME !! Tender/Juicy Pork Chops are not easy to cook perfectly by any means. THIS recipe however is dummy proof and they are perfect every time and believe me, I have cooked pork chops every possible way during my lifetime. The onion is totally optional and does not effect the tenderness or juiciness of the chops, it ONLY changes the flavor and we love them both ways. The only thing I do different from the recipe is that I use either beef or chicken broth in place of the water and I use fresh cracked pepper and garlic powder along with the season salt. Awesome flavor.

This is a basic recipe that I've used for years. The only difference is I brine it for about a half an hour in saltwater. Also, I sift flour on top of and in the water which helps it make its own gravy. It's a good old standby! Thanks for sharing!
Pork chop was stilll tuff. After experimenting, I cooked 2hrs at 300 F. Braising at lower temp was better. Still looking for a fork tender moist chop recipe tho
Pork chops were so tender. Loved this method. Reminded me of a friend from long ago who told me the onions cried onto the pork chops and made them tender.

This recipe is great. I had a 6 pack of "assorted" chops all bone in. Brined for 2 hours before using recipe and used beef broth instead of water, but skipped the seasoning salt. The cooking method itself was perfect. Chops were super flavorful, tender and moist. Thanks for sharing!
